Built **real-time financial charts**, detailed finance panels and payment-service-provider integrations, including a **dedicated WebSocket support chat** and custom tools developed in-house.

Improved role-aware routing, network requests and caching; strengthened Nginx and payment-facing protections against **CSRF, XSS, clickjacking and unsafe CORS**, alongside architectural reviews and mentorship.

caseStudy.title: Frontend leadership for a financial platform
caseStudy.caption: Public project capture. Private application screens and confidential product details are not published.

sections.title: Product context
paragraphs: Multi-role financial applications require shared architecture, secure access and reliable updates across browser and installed clients. I joined Hesabo in August 2025 and became Frontend Chapter Lead in April 2026.

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: I led reusable UI, business-logic and design-system refactoring, configurable layouts and mobile-ready panels. The supplied résumé reports a 17% smaller bundle and 9% better initial-load performance for this refactor.

I develop architecture-aware Claude/Codex agents and automate validation with Cypress E2E, integration and mock tests. I also work on role-aware routing, caching, Nginx and payment security, architectural reviews and mentorship.

My Hesabo work also covers real-time financial charts, detailed financial panels, payment-service-provider integrations and a dedicated support chat room built with WebSockets and our custom in-house tools.

sections.title: Evidence and scope
paragraphs: Earlier, I developed seven role-based React/TypeScript/Vite/MobX applications and shipped Capacitor Android builds and PWAs. The public image is the company website, not the private financial applications.

The résumé is the source of the refactor figures; this portfolio does not independently remeasure employer systems. Product-aware Figma-to-code and feature-branch testing workflows are described at capability level without confidential implementation details.

sections.title: Product context
paragraphs: An early MVP of a broader confidential platform. The public boutique explores garment discovery, catalog information and photographic outfit previews.

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: I built the Next.js/TypeScript application and Three.js/React Three Fiber environment, with HTML browsing controls, reduced-motion handling and WebGL fallbacks.
Compact garment images precede focused full-resolution assets. Catalog requests use bounded upstream access and caching; unavailable or expired stock and price information is cleared.
